finding: §3 repairs round 4's missing-marker finding by naming a marker that already exists for a DIFFERENT release, so the prospectivity rule is a no-op and the reset is retroactive after all. `engine.IsLegacyRound` is `return r.IDScheme == ""` (internal/engine/reviewstate.go:503-505), and `IDScheme` is stamped `engine.IDSchemeSlug` by internal/cli/audit_record.go:213 on EVERY audit round recorded since v0.30.0 — its own struct comment (reviewstate.go:28-34) says so: 'Value "slug" for an audit round recorded under v0.30.0+ ... empty on a legacy round recorded before this release', where 'this release' is v0.30.0. Measured on the very corpus §3 argues from: all nine audit rounds in spec/.tp-review/0.35.0/state.json carry "id_scheme": "slug", so `IsLegacyRound` is false for every one and §3's rule — 'applies the reset only from the first marked round onward' — starts at round 1. Their spec_hashes are r1=r2=a46f45c6, r3=c06544ea, r4=50be1428, r5=2dd780c6, r6=6f42a8eb, r7=r8=1259a4af, r9=54e031e6; the only two clean rounds are r8 and r9 and the hash moves between them, so `ConsecutiveCleanSince` returns 1 and at audit_clean_rounds 2 `ConvergedSince` is false. A converged, shipped cycle reports converged:false the moment this release installs — the exact retroactive outcome §3's 'Why the word alone will not do' paragraph says the marker prevents. The marker also cannot be repurposed: it is recorded on audit rounds only (reviewstate.go:33-34, asserted by cli/idscheme_marker_test.go:49), so a review-side reader of the same field would see every round as legacy.
suggestion: This release needs its own marker, not v0.30.0's. Add a per-round field stamped by --record from v0.37.0 forward (e.g. `hash_reset: true`, or a `recorded_by` version string) and state that the walk cuts at a boundary only when the NEWER of the two adjacent rounds carries it, so no history recorded before the upgrade can ever cut. Then state, as the worked example §3 already uses, what the reset returns on v0.35.0's nine rounds under the new marker (it must be the pre-reset 2, not 1). If reusing IsLegacyRound is genuinely intended, §3 must say that the reset applies to every audit round recorded since v0.30.0 and own the v0.35.0 regression as the release's stated behaviour.

finding: Test 10's named killing mutation cannot fail, so the test passes against an implementation that omits the mechanism §3 exists to add. Test 10: 'The mutation that kills it: dropping the `IsLegacyRound` check, which makes v0.35.0's recorded history report `all` as never-converged.' Measured: all nine audit rounds in spec/.tp-review/0.35.0/state.json carry "id_scheme": "slug", so `IsLegacyRound` (reviewstate.go:503-505, `r.IDScheme == ""`) returns FALSE for every one of them with the check in place. Keeping the check and dropping it therefore produce identical answers on the named input, and that answer is the mutant's answer — never-converged — in both. §5's own opening promise ('Every test names the input that makes it fail, because four earlier drafts of this list contained a test that passed against unmodified tp') is the rule this test breaks, and CLAUDE.md states it generally: the informative experiment is the one that could have failed. Test 10's other half is unwritable for the same reason: 'a history recorded before the upgrade keeps the `consecutive_clean` it had' has no instance in this repository, because no audit round tp has ever recorded lacks the marker — only a synthesised `ReviewRound{IDScheme: ""}` sequence exhibits the case, and a synthesised marker-less round is by construction a round no --record of any tp version produces on the audit path.
suggestion: Split test 10 into the two things it conflates. (a) A unit-level assertion over synthesised rounds — `ConsecutiveCleanSince` on `[{IDScheme:"", SpecHash:A, Clean:true}, {IDScheme:"", SpecHash:B, Clean:true}]` returns 2 while the same pair with the v0.37.0 marker returns 1 — which is a mutation the IsLegacyRound check actually survives. (b) A stated expected value on v0.35.0's real nine rounds, whose id_scheme is `slug` throughout; whatever §3's marker turns out to be, that is the number the release regresses or preserves, and it is the one an operator will notice first.

finding: §2 states the predicate over round cleanliness alone and never says whether `audit_converge_on` reaches the three other derived values `tp audit --record` emits from the same rows, all of which are severity-blind today. internal/engine/rolestreaks.go:128-142 `auditRoundOpenByRole` tallies a role's open rows through `AuditRowIsPass` and reads no severity at all; `RoleStreak.Open` and `RoleStreak.ConsecutiveClean` come from that tally (rolestreaks.go:107-108), and engine/speccoverage.go's `SpecCoverageCleanRounds` is derived from those streaks. So under `blocking`, an unchanged implementation records a round `clean: true` while the SAME payload reports `role_streaks: [{role: maintainability-conventions, consecutive_clean: 0, open: 3}]` and `spec_coverage_clean_rounds` unchanged. I cannot write acceptance for §2's task without that decision, and it is not cosmetic in either direction: Non-Goal 1's argument ('a severity-parity `--check` still exits 1 for exactly the rounds the gap is about') presupposes severity parity reaching the streak surface, while §2's text confines the field to `clean`. §2's own touch list ('16 production `.go` files') is the review-side count and contains neither rolestreaks.go nor speccoverage.go, because `review_converge_on` has no per-role streak surface to reach — so the audit twin's surface is strictly larger than the number §2 sizes it by.
suggestion: State it in §2 in one sentence, and give it a test. Either: '`audit_converge_on` scopes the round-level `clean` predicate only — `role_streaks`, `spec_coverage_clean_rounds` and `divergence` keep counting every non-`PASS` row, so a clean round under `blocking` can carry a non-zero `open`', with a §5 test asserting exactly that pairing so the apparent contradiction is pinned as intended; or 'the same predicate governs `auditRoundOpenByRole`', in which case add engine/rolestreaks.go and engine/speccoverage.go to the touch list and say what `spec_coverage_clean_rounds` means once it counts only blocking rows.

finding: §2 and §5 test 11 fence one of the two commands that can write the field, and the unfenced one is the command §4's own guard test drives. `fenceWorkflowWrite` has exactly four call sites: internal/cli/set.go:414 and :428, and internal/cli/set_project.go:98 and :108. Every one of the four sits INSIDE a branch that has already parsed the value with `strconv.ParseFloat` or `strconv.Atoi` — which is what 'numeric by signature' costs in practice: a string-valued field reaches none of them, and 'widening that fence to string fields' is therefore not one edit but two new call sites in two different files, in the string branch of each. §2 names only `tp set --workflow audit_converge_on=blocking` and §5 test 11 pins only that form. `tp set --workflow --project audit_converge_on=blocking` writes the project layer, which §2's own precedence chain says the resolver reads, and it is the exact invocation at internal/cli/audit_signal_test.go:472 that §4 says this release reverses. A unit under `tp run` that takes the `--project` route relaxes its own audit gate and no test in §5 catches it.
suggestion: Say both forms in §2 ('`tp set --workflow audit_converge_on=blocking` and its `--project` form both exit 2 under TP_UNATTENDED=1 with the escalation hint'), name the two string branches — set.go's and set_project.go's — as the sites, since the four existing numeric sites cannot be reached by a string field, and make §5 test 11 assert both forms plus exit 0 for each without the variable. Also name the `--decision` slug the hint tells the unit to escalate under: `escalationDecision` (unattended.go:19-27) maps only review_max_rounds and audit_max_rounds and returns "other" for everything else, so the release either accepts "other" or adds a name, and §5 test 11 asserts a hint string either way.

finding: Test 6's frozen fixture is specified as fields that cannot produce the value test 6 asserts. It says the testdata is 'the `(status, severity)` pairs of v0.35.0's nine recorded rounds', and then asserts that '`blocking` converges at round 3 and `all` at round 9'. Converging is a claim about `engine.Converged`, which is `ConsecutiveClean(rounds) >= requiredCleanRounds && !StateStale(rounds, currentHash)` (engine/reviewstate.go:509-511), and `StateStale` (:443-448) reads `rounds[len-1].SpecHash`. A (status, severity) pair carries no `spec_hash`, so the copied fixture can compute `ConsecutiveClean` and nothing else. §3 then makes the same fixture need a third field: `ConsecutiveCleanSince` compares each round's `spec_hash` and consults `IsLegacyRound`, which reads `id_scheme`. Test 6 also never says which walk it replays through. That is load-bearing rather than pedantic: v0.35.0's real hashes put r8 at 1259a4af and r9 at 54e031e6, so replayed through `ConvergedSince` with the real hashes `all` does NOT converge at round 9, and test 6 contradicts §5 test 8 and §2.1's table on the same committed data.
suggestion: Specify the fixture's whole shape: per round, the rows' `(status, severity)` plus that round's `spec_hash` and `id_scheme`, copied verbatim from spec/.tp-review/0.35.0/state.json at the cited commit; state the `currentHash` the replay passes (round 9's own hash, or `StateStale` alone decides the answer); and state explicitly whether test 6 replays through `Converged` or `ConvergedSince`. If it is `Converged`, say so and say that test 6 therefore measures §2 with §3 switched off — otherwise the two halves of this release disagree about the same nine rounds.

finding: Test 9 now has a signature to test against but does not bind the argument the signature added, and three different bindings give three different answers. §3 declares `engine.ConsecutiveCleanSince(rounds []ReviewRound, current string) int`; test 9 says 'ConsecutiveCleanSince on rounds at hashes A, A, B returns **1** — the trailing run'. That is 1 only when `current` is B. Passed A it is 0 (the newest round's hash already differs from `current`, so the walk stops before counting anything); passed the empty string, or the live spec's hash when the spec has moved since the last recorded round — the ordinary mid-loop state, and the state this very spec is in — it is also 0. Test 7 pins its own fixture's binding explicitly ('this fixture's **last** round's `spec_hash` equals the current spec hash') and test 9 does not, so two tests in the same list use different conventions for the same parameter and only one of them states it. The choice also decides whether `ConsecutiveCleanSince` is anything more than `ConsecutiveClean` plus the `StateStale` term `Converged` already ANDs in.
suggestion: Bind it: 'with `current` = B, `ConsecutiveCleanSince` returns 1; `ConsecutiveClean` on the same input returns 3.' Then add the one fixture that separates the two readings, which §5 still has no test for: rounds A, A both clean with `current` = C (a spec edited since the last recorded round), where the trailing-run reading returns 2 and the live-spec reading returns 0. Whichever is intended, the printed `consecutive_clean` differs, and §3 says changing that printed integer is the point.

finding: §2.2's closing sentence points at the wrong test after §5 was rewritten from nine tests to twelve. It reads '§5 test 4 uses a legacy row because it is convenient and real, not because the case is live.' §5 test 4 is '**`warning` is advisory**' and involves no legacy row at all. The test that uses one is §5 test 5 ('Unrecognised fails closed'), whose own text says 'a legacy row supplies only (a) — all 67 carry a present, non-null `high`/`medium`/`low`.' A decomposer following §2.2 to find test 4's fixture rationale finds a test about `warning` counts instead, and the sentence that justifies the whole 67-row section lands on nothing.
suggestion: Change '§5 test 4' to '§5 test 5'. And sweep the file's other §-plus-number references while the renumbering is fresh — §5 test 7's 'satisfies test 8' and §4's 'Non-Goal 2 keeps the first two true' both still resolve correctly, so this and §4's closing reference are the two that moved.

finding: §4's guard-reversal paragraph ends on a reference the §5 rewrite invalidated: 'Non-Goal 2 keeps the first two true; §5 test 9 pins all nine.' §5 test 9 is '**The shared walk does not move**' — `ConsecutiveCleanSince` on hashes A, A, B — and pins none of `TestAuditGate_NoEscapeHatchFromTheGate`'s assertions. The test that pins them is §5 test 12 ('**The nine surviving assertions** of `TestAuditGate_NoEscapeHatchFromTheGate` still pass, including `:498`'s streak-entry shape'). This matters more than a numbering slip because §4's paragraph exists precisely to stop a unit deleting those nine assertions under cover of 'reversing the guard', and it points that unit at a test about a different subject. (The counts in the paragraph are correct as re-measured: internal/cli/audit_signal_test.go:469-503 carries exactly eleven assert/require calls — :473, :474, :481, :484, :485, :490, :493, :494, :497, :498, :500 — and :473-474 are the pair the release reverses, leaving nine.)
suggestion: Change '§5 test 9' to '§5 test 12'. Since the paragraph's whole job is to name what a unit may not delete, consider naming the assertions by line as well as by count — :481/:484 are `require` calls whose failure aborts the test before the nine are reached, so 'all nine still pass' is only observable if the reversal at :472-474 leaves the fixture in the state those two requires expect.

finding: §2's evidence for the precedence repair is a recipe that writing it down made false. 'a repo-wide search for `TP_REVIEW_CONVERGE_ON` returns zero'. Run today from the repository root it returns six matches in five files: CLAUDE.md:329 (the same claim, added by the same repair), spec/0.37.0.md:32 (this sentence), spec/.tp-review/0.37.0/snapshot-round-5.md:32, and two review artifacts — spec/.tp-review/0.37.0/review-round-4.ndjson and review-r4-architect.ndjson, where round 4's architect finding cites the identical search. The substance is correct and I re-verified it independently: engine/configresolve.go:251-269 merges exactly two layers over the default for every field, ReviewConvergeOn at :261, and no Go file anywhere reads such a variable. But an implementer who runs the recipe as written sees six hits and cannot tell a refutation from a self-reference — CLAUDE.md's own rule is that a claim bound to a named artifact cannot rot silently, and a corpus-wide grep is the opposite of that.
suggestion: Scope the search to the code it is a claim about: 'a search for `TP_REVIEW_CONVERGE_ON` under `internal/` returns zero'. That stays true however many specs and round files quote it, and it is the set the claim is actually about.

finding: Five conclusions formed this round and dropped before recording, plus the round-4 findings I re-measured as repaired. (1) I drafted that §5 test 12's reversal contaminates the nine surviving assertions: if :472-474 is inverted so `tp set --workflow --project audit_converge_on=blocking` SUCCEEDS, the rest of the test runs under `blocking`, and :485-487 asserts go-safety carries `{consecutive_clean: 0, open: 1}` while :489-490 asserts `--check` exits 1. I checked the fixture rather than assuming: `signalRow` (audit_signal_test.go:40-42) emits `{"item_id":...,"role":...,"status":"FAIL"}` with NO severity key, so §2's fail-closed rule grades it blocking and the round stays non-clean; and `role_streaks` is severity-blind anyway (rolestreaks.go:138). The nine survive. The dependency is real but the outcome is not a defect, so only the part that IS a property of the text — the wrong test number — was recorded, at §4. (2) I drafted that §3's `Converged` call-site list omits `engine/resume.go`; it does not — resume.go:87 is `Converged(auditRounds, ...)` and is cited exactly. I also checked the other five: audit_record.go:95 and :333, run_status.go:149, budget.go:26, review_status.go:67, and the `ConsecutiveClean` list audit.go:352 / audit_record.go:101 / :339 / review_status.go:91. Every citation in §3 is correct. (3) I drafted that `run_status.go:149` serves both phases and so cannot move to `ConvergedSince` without breaking Non-Goal 4; it is inside `addAuditSignals` over `st.AuditRounds` (run_status.go:127-150), audit-only. No finding. (4) I drafted that §5 test 6's replay cannot be built over a mutable corpus; that is round 4's own unresolved `replay-gate-over-a-mutable-corpus` and the testdata half is now repaired, so only the new part — the fixture's fields cannot produce a `Converged` answer — was recorded. (5) I re-measured three repaired claims rather than inheriting round 4's verdicts, and all three now hold: §1's round count is 9 (was 22); §2's touch surface is exactly 16 production `.go` files and 11 test files, counted; and §5 test 4's '158 of the corpus's 360 non-`PASS` rows' is exact — 158 `warning` rows across the audit-round files (44 in v0.36.0, 22 in v0.35.0, 45 in v0.33.0, 15 in v0.34.0, 11 in v0.24.0, 10 in v0.32.0, 6 in v0.31.2, 2 each in v0.25.0 and v0.28.0, 1 in v0.26.0), 135 `error`+`info`, and 293 + §2.2's 67 out-of-enum = 360.
suggestion: No action beyond the rows recorded. The habit that paid this round: when a repair names an existing helper as the fix for a missing mechanism, read the helper's own definition and its stamping site before accepting it — `IsLegacyRound` reads as exactly right in §3's prose and is a marker for a release seven versions back, which only its one-line body and audit_record.go:213 reveal.
